119	        plan_path = self._split_path(name)
120	        if plan_path.exists():
121	            existing = self._read_split(plan_path)
122	            if self._same_inputs(existing, seed, fraction_ratios, snapshot):
123	                return SplitPlanResult(name=name, created=False, plan=existing)
124	            raise SplitError(
125	                f"Split plan {name!r} already exists with different seed, "
126	                "ratios or samples; choose another name"
127	            )
128	
129	        self._write_json_atomic(plan_path, plan_payload)
130	        return SplitPlanResult(name=name, created=True, plan=plan_payload)
131	
132	    def get_split(self, name: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
133	        """Return the stored plan payload, or raise if it does not exist."""
134	        validate_name(name)
135	        plan_path = self._split_path(name)
136	        if not plan_path.exists():
137	            raise SplitError(f"Split plan not found: {name}")
138	        return self._read_split(plan_path)
139	
140	    def _split_path(self, name: str) -> Path:
141	        # validate_name() has already ruled out path separators and "..".
142	        return self.splits_directory / f"{name}.json"
143	
144	    def _build_plan(
145	        self,
146	        name: str,
147	        seed: int,
148	        ratios: tuple[Fraction, Fraction, Fraction],
149	        snapshot: list[dict[str, Any]],
150	        assignment: dict[str, str],
151	    ) -> dict[str, Any]:
152	        sets = {set_name: [] for set_name in SET_NAMES}
153	        for sample in snapshot:
154	            set_name = assignment[sample["sha256"]]
155	            sets[set_name].append(
156	                {
157	                    "sha256": sample["sha256"],
158	                    "label": category_name(category_key(sample["label"])),
159	                    "source": sample["source"],
160	                }
161	            )
162	
163	        set_summaries: dict[str, Any] = {}
164	        for set_name in SET_NAMES:
165	            members = sets[set_name]
166	            distribution = Counter(member["label"] for member in members)
167	            set_summaries[set_name] = {
168	                "samples": len(members),
169	                "distribution": dict(sorted(distribution.items())),
170	                "members": [
171	                    {
172	                        "sha256": member["sha256"],
173	                        "label": member["label"],
174	                        "source": member["source"],
175	                    }
176	                    for member in members
177	                ],
178	            }
179	
180	        overall = Counter(
181	            category_name(category_key(sample["label"])) for sample in snapshot
182	        )
183	        return {
184	            "schema_version": SPLIT_SCHEMA_VERSION,
185	            "name": name,
186	            "seed": seed,
187	            "ratios": {
188	                set_name: str(ratios[i]) for i, set_name in enumerate(SET_NAMES)
189	            },
190	            "samples": {
191	                "total": len(snapshot),
192	                "distribution": dict(sorted(overall.items())),
193	            },
194	            "sets": set_summaries,
195	        }
196	
197	    @staticmethod
198	    def _same_inputs(
199	        existing: dict[str, Any],
200	        seed: int,
201	        ratios: tuple[Fraction, Fraction, Fraction],
202	        snapshot: list[dict[str, Any]],
203	    ) -> bool:
204	        """Whether a stored plan was created from the exact same inputs."""
205	        if existing.get("seed") != seed:
206	            return False
207	        stored_ratios = existing.get("ratios")
208	        if not isinstance(stored_ratios, dict):
209	            return False
210	        for i, set_name in enumerate(SET_NAMES):
211	            stored = stored_ratios.get(set_name)
212	            if not isinstance(stored, str) or Fraction(stored) != ratios[i]:
213	                return False
214	
215	        # Reuse requires the exact same sample identities with the exact
216	        # same creation-time labels; recorded sources are informational and
217	        # do not participate in the identity (the snapshot itself is the
218	        # decision input, per the feature contract).
219	        current = sorted(
220	            (sample["sha256"], category_name(category_key(sample.get("label"))))
221	            for sample in snapshot
222	        )
223	        stored: list[tuple[str, str]] = []
224	        sets = existing["sets"]
225	        for set_name in SET_NAMES:
226	            for member in sets[set_name]["members"]:
227	                stored.append((member["sha256"], member.get("label")))
228	        return sorted(stored) == current
229	
230	    def _read_split(self, plan_path: Path) -> dict[str, Any]:
231	        try:
232	            data = json.loads(plan_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
233	        except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError) as error:
234	            raise SplitError(f"Cannot read split plan: {error}") from error
235	        self._validate_split_payload(data)
236	        return data
237	
238	    @staticmethod
239	    def _validate_split_payload(data: Any) -> None:
240	        if not isinstance(data, dict):
241	            raise SplitError("Split plan record is malformed")
242	        if data.get("schema_version") != SPLIT_SCHEMA_VERSION:
243	            raise SplitError("Unsupported split plan schema version")
244	        if not isinstance(data.get("name"), str):
245	            raise SplitError("Split plan record is missing its name")
246	        if not isinstance(data.get("seed"), int) or isinstance(data.get("seed"), bool):
247	            raise SplitError("Split plan record is missing its seed")
248	        ratios = data.get("ratios")
249	        if not isinstance(ratios, dict):
250	            raise SplitError("Split plan record is missing its ratios")
251	        ratio_values = []
252	        for set_name in SET_NAMES:
253	            value = ratios.get(set_name)
254	            if not isinstance(value, str):
255	                raise SplitError(f"Split plan record is missing ratio for {set_name}")
256	            ratio_values.append(value)
257	        try:
258	            validate_ratios(ratio_values)
259	        except SplitError as error:
260	            raise SplitError(f"Split plan record has invalid ratios: {error}") from error
261	
262	        samples = data.get("samples")
263	        if (
264	            not isinstance(samples, dict)
265	            or not isinstance(samples.get("total"), int)
266	            or isinstance(samples.get("total"), bool)
267	        ):
268	            raise SplitError("Split plan record is missing its sample summary")
269	        if not isinstance(samples.get("distribution"), dict):
270	            raise SplitError("Split plan record is missing its class distribution")
271	        sets = data.get("sets")
272	        if not isinstance(sets, dict):
273	            raise SplitError("Split plan record is missing its set assignments")
274	
275	        seen: set[str] = set()
276	        overall: Counter[str] = Counter()
277	        for set_name in SET_NAMES:
278	            set_payload = sets.get(set_name)
279	            if not isinstance(set_payload, dict):
280	                raise SplitError(f"Split plan record is missing set {set_name}")
281	            members = set_payload.get("members")
282	            if not isinstance(members, list):
283	                raise SplitError(f"Split plan record is missing members for {set_name}")
284	            if set_payload.get("samples") != len(members):
285	                raise SplitError(f"Split plan record has a bad count for {set_name}")
286	            distribution = Counter()
287	            for member in members:
288	                if (
289	                    not isinstance(member, dict)
290	                    or not isinstance(member.get("sha256"), str)
291	                    or not isinstance(member.get("label"), str)
292	                    or not isinstance(member.get("source"), str)
293	                ):
294	                    raise SplitError(f"Split plan record has a bad member in {set_name}")
295	                digest = member["sha256"]
296	                if digest in seen:
297	                    raise SplitError(
298	                        f"Split plan record lists {digest} in more than one set"
299	                    )
300	                seen.add(digest)
301	                distribution[member["label"]] += 1
302	                overall[member["label"]] += 1
303	            if dict(sorted(distribution.items())) != {
304	                key: value for key, value in sorted(set_payload.get("distribution", {}).items())
305	            }:
306	                raise SplitError(
307	                    f"Split plan record has a mismatched distribution for {set_name}"
308	                )
309	        if samples["total"] != len(seen):
310	            raise SplitError("Split plan record has a mismatched sample total")
311	        if dict(sorted(overall.items())) != {
312	            key: value for key, value in sorted(samples["distribution"].items())
313	        }:
314	            raise SplitError("Split plan record has a mismatched class distribution")
315	
316	    def _write_json_atomic(self, path: Path, payload: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
317	        """Write via a temp file + fsync + atomic replace.
318	
319	        A reader therefore observes either no plan or the complete plan,
320	        never a partial one.
321	        """
322	        path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
323	        temporary = path.with_name(f".{path.name}.tmp")
324	        try:
325	            with temporary.open("w", encoding="utf-8") as stream:
326	                stream.write(json.dumps(payload, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2) + "\n")
327	                stream.flush()
328	                os.fsync(stream.fileno())
329	            os.replace(temporary, path)
330	            self._fsync_directory(path.parent)
331	        except OSError:
332	            temporary.unlink(missing_ok=True)
333	            raise
334	
335	    @staticmethod
336	    def _fsync_directory(directory: Path) -> None:
337	        try:
338	            descriptor = os.open(directory, os.O_RDONLY)
339	        except OSError:
340	            return
341	        try:
342	            os.fsync(descriptor)
343	        except OSError:
344	            pass
345	        finally:
346	            os.close(descriptor)
347	
348	    def _read(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
349	        try:
350	            data = json.loads(self.manifest_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
351	        except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError) as error:
352	            raise ValueError(f"Cannot read dataset manifest: {error}") from error
353	        if data.get("schema_version") != 1 or not isinstance(data.get("items"), list):
354	            raise ValueError("Unsupported dataset manifest")
355	        return data
356	
357	    def _write(self, data: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
358	        temporary = self.manifest_path.with_suffix(".tmp")
359	        temporary.write_text(
360	            json.dumps(data, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2) + "\n",
361	            encoding="utf-8",
362	        )
363	        temporary.replace(self.manifest_path)
364	
365	    @staticmethod
366	    def _digest(path: Path) -> str:
367	        hasher = hashlib.sha256()
368	        with path.open("rb") as stream:
369	            for chunk in iter(lambda: stream.read(1024 * 1024), b""):
370	                hasher.update(chunk)
371	        return hasher.hexdigest()

1	"""Stratified train/validation/test split planning.
2	
3	A plan allocates every sample to exactly one of three sets.  Exact rational
4	arithmetic (:mod:`fractions`) drives the allocation so that, for every
5	class *and* for the dataset as a whole, each set's sample count differs
6	from its proportional expectation by strictly less than one.
7	
8	Assignments derive solely from sample identities (content digests), labels
9	and the integer seed, so they are independent of import order, manifest
10	ordering, workspace location and process restarts.
11	"""
12	
13	from __future__ import annotations
14	
15	import hashlib
16	import math
17	from fractions import Fraction
18	from typing import Any, Sequence
19	
20	# Sentinel for samples without a label.  An object (not the string
21	# "unlabeled") keeps a real class literally named "unlabeled" separate.
22	UNLABELED = object()
23	
24	SET_NAMES = ("train", "validation", "test")
25	
26	
27	class SplitError(ValueError):
28	    """A split parameter or record is invalid."""
29	
30	
31	def category_key(label: Any) -> Any:
32	    """Stratum key for a manifest label value.
33	
34	    ``None`` and the empty string both mean "unlabeled", matching
35	    :meth:`DatasetStore.summary`; any other label is taken literally.
36	    """
37	    if label is None or label == "":
38	        return UNLABELED
39	    return label
40	
41	
42	def category_name(key: Any) -> str:
43	    """Render a stratum key for JSON output.
44	
45	    The unlabeled stratum renders as the empty string (which mirrors the
46	    manifest's empty-label meaning); a genuine class literally named
47	    ``"unlabeled"`` therefore stays distinguishable.
48	    """
49	    return "" if key is UNLABELED else str(key)
50	
51	
52	def _sort_key(key: Any) -> tuple[int, str]:
53	    return (0 if key is UNLABELED else 1, category_name(key))
54	
55	
56	def validate_name(name: str) -> str:
57	    if not isinstance(name, str) or not name.strip():
58	        raise SplitError("Split plan name must not be empty or only whitespace")
59	    if "/" in name or "\\" in name:
60	        raise SplitError("Split plan name must not contain '/' or '\\'")
61	    if name in (".", ".."):
62	        raise SplitError("Split plan name must not be '.' or '..'")
63	    return name
64	
65	
66	def parse_ratio(value: Any) -> Fraction:
67	    """Parse one ratio as a finite number in the closed interval [0, 1]."""
68	    if isinstance(value, bool):
69	        raise SplitError(f"Ratio must be a number, got {value!r}")
70	    if isinstance(value, float):
71	        if not math.isfinite(value):
72	            raise SplitError(f"Ratio must be finite, got {value!r}")
73	        # Use the shortest decimal that round-trips, so 0.1 means 1/10
74	        # rather than its binary approximation.
75	        value = repr(value)
76	    try:
77	        if isinstance(value, Fraction):
78	            ratio = value
79	        elif isinstance(value, int):
80	            ratio = Fraction(value)
81	        elif isinstance(value, str):
82	            ratio = Fraction(value)
83	        else:
84	            raise SplitError(f"Ratio must be a number, got {value!r}")
85	    except (ValueError, ZeroDivisionError, ArithmeticError, OverflowError):
86	        raise SplitError(f"Ratio must be a finite number, got {value!r}") from None
87	    if ratio < 0 or ratio > 1:
88	        raise SplitError(
89	            f"Ratio must be between 0 and 1 (inclusive), got {value!r}"
90	        )
91	    return ratio
92	
93	
94	def validate_ratios(ratios: Sequence[Any]) -> tuple[Fraction, Fraction, Fraction]:
95	    if len(ratios) != 3:
96	        raise SplitError("Exactly three ratios (train, validation, test) are required")
97	    parsed = tuple(parse_ratio(value) for value in ratios)
98	    if sum(parsed, Fraction(0)) != 1:
99	        raise SplitError("Ratios must sum to exactly 1")
100	    return parsed  # type: ignore[return-value]
101	
102	
103	def allocation_table(
104	    strata_counts: dict[Any, int], ratios: tuple[Fraction, Fraction, Fraction]
105	) -> dict[Any, tuple[int, int, int]]:
106	    """Allocate integer ``(train, validation, test)`` counts per stratum.
107	
108	    Construction: every cell starts at ``floor(N_c * p_s)``; each stratum
109	    then distributes its leftover free units (at most two per row) and each
110	    column total must land on ``floor`` or ``ceil`` of its own expectation.
111	    A free unit may only enter a non-integral cell.  An integral placement
112	    always exists (controlled rounding of the fractional-parts table); the
113	    small max-flow below searches the deterministic floor/ceil choices.
114	    Every used cell ends at ``floor`` or ``ceil`` of its expectation and
115	    every column total at ``floor``/``ceil`` of its, hence every
116	    discrepancy is strictly below one.
117	    """
118	    strata = sorted(strata_counts, key=_sort_key)
119	    total = sum(strata_counts.values())
120	
121	    floors: dict[Any, list[int]] = {}
122	    parts: dict[Any, list[Fraction]] = {}
123	    for c in strata:
124	        expectation = [Fraction(strata_counts[c]) * ratios[j] for j in range(3)]
125	        floors[c] = [e.numerator // e.denominator for e in expectation]
126	        parts[c] = [e - floors[c][j] for j, e in enumerate(expectation)]
127	
128	    # Fractional column sums S_j; a column receives floor(S_j) or
129	    # ceil(S_j) free units.  sum_j S_j is the integer number of free
130	    # units, so the fractional parts sum to an integer k: exactly k
131	    # non-integral columns round up.  A column whose S_j is integral
132	    # cannot round up (that would be a discrepancy of exactly one), so
133	    # the size-k subsets are tried until a flow matches every row.
134	    column_sums = [sum((parts[c][j] for c in strata), Fraction(0)) for j in range(3)]
135	    column_base = [s.numerator // s.denominator for s in column_sums]
136	    row_supply = {c: int(sum(parts[c])) for c in strata}
137	    extra_needed = sum(row_supply.values()) - sum(column_base)
138	    eligible = [j for j in range(3) if column_sums[j] != column_base[j]]
139	
140	    flows = _controlled_rounding(
141	        strata, parts, row_supply, column_base, extra_needed, eligible
142	    )
143	
144	    table: dict[Any, tuple[int, int, int]] = {}
145	    for c in strata:
146	        table[c] = tuple(floors[c][j] + flows[c][j] for j in range(3))  # type: ignore[assignment]
147	        if sum(table[c]) != strata_counts[c]:
148	            raise SplitError("Internal error: stratum count mismatch")  # pragma: no cover
149	    for j in range(3):
150	        column_total = sum(table[c][j] for c in strata)
151	        expect_total = Fraction(total) * ratios[j]
152	        if abs(Fraction(column_total) - expect_total) >= 1:
153	            raise SplitError("Internal error: total count mismatch")  # pragma: no cover
154	    return table
155	
156	
157	def _controlled_rounding(
158	    strata: Sequence[Any],
159	    parts: dict[Any, list[Fraction]],
160	    row_supply: dict[Any, int],
161	    column_base: list[int],
162	    extra_needed: int,
163	    eligible: Sequence[int],
164	) -> dict[Any, list[int]]:
165	    """Place every row's free units on non-integral cells.
166	
167	    Column j receives ``column_base[j]`` units, plus one for each member
168	    of a size-``extra_needed`` subset of eligible columns (its total then
169	    rounds ``S_j`` to floor or ceil).  Candidate subsets are tried in a
170	    fixed order; the fractional parts themselves prove the rounded
171	    polytope has an integral vertex, so one candidate always yields a
172	    full-value flow.
173	    """
174	    from itertools import combinations
175	
176	    if extra_needed == 0:
177	        candidates: list[tuple[int, ...]] = [()]
178	    else:
179	        candidates = list(combinations(eligible, extra_needed))
180	
181	    last_error: Exception | None = None
182	    for extra in candidates:
183	        demand = column_base[:]
184	        for j in extra:
185	            demand[j] += 1
186	        try:
187	            return _integral_flow(strata, parts, row_supply, demand)
188	        except SplitError as error:  # candidate infeasible, try next
189	            last_error = error
190	    raise SplitError(
191	        f"Internal error: cannot satisfy split proportions: {last_error}"
192	    )  # pragma: no cover
193	
194	
195	def _integral_flow(
196	    strata: Sequence[Any],
197	    parts: dict[Any, list[Fraction]],
198	    row_supply: dict[Any, int],
199	    column_demand: list[int],
200	) -> dict[Any, list[int]]:
201	    """Max-flow placement; raises unless every free unit is placed."""
202	    source = ("s",)
203	    sink = ("t",)
204	    row_nodes = [("r", i) for i in range(len(strata))]
205	    col_nodes = [("c", j) for j in range(3)]
206	    residual: dict[Any, dict[Any, int]] = {source: {}, sink: {}}
207	    for node in row_nodes + col_nodes:
208	        residual[node] = {}
209	
210	    def add_edge(u: Any, v: Any, capacity: int) -> None:
211	        residual[u][v] = capacity
212	        residual[v].setdefault(u, 0)
213	
214	    required = 0
215	    for i, c in enumerate(strata):
216	        supply = row_supply[c]
217	        required += supply
218	        if supply:
219	            add_edge(source, row_nodes[i], supply)
220	        for j in sorted(range(3), key=lambda k: (-parts[c][k], k)):
221	            if parts[c][j] > 0:
222	                add_edge(row_nodes[i], col_nodes[j], 1)
223	    for j, node in enumerate(col_nodes):
224	        add_edge(node, sink, column_demand[j])
225	
226	    pushed = 0
227	    while pushed < required:
228	        path = _augmenting_path(residual, source, sink, row_nodes, col_nodes)
229	        if path is None:
230	            raise SplitError("no feasible integral placement")
231	        for u, v in zip(path, path[1:]):
232	            residual[u][v] -= 1
233	            residual[v][u] += 1
234	        pushed += 1
235	
236	    flows = {c: [0, 0, 0] for c in strata}
237	    for i, c in enumerate(strata):
238	        for j, col in enumerate(col_nodes):
239	            # Forward edge capacity was 1; residual reverse flow of 1
240	            # means the unit was placed in this cell.
241	            flows[c][j] = residual[col].get(row_nodes[i], 0)
242	    return flows
243	
244	
245	def _augmenting_path(
246	    residual: dict[Any, dict[Any, int]],
247	    source: Any,
248	    sink: Any,
249	    row_nodes: Sequence[Any],
250	    col_nodes: Sequence[Any],
251	) -> list[Any] | None:
252	    """Breadth-first augmenting path with fixed node traversal order."""
253	    order = [source, *row_nodes, *col_nodes, sink]
254	    previous: dict[Any, Any] = {source: None}
255	    queue = [source]
256	    head = 0
257	    while head < len(queue):
258	        node = queue[head]
259	        head += 1
260	        for neighbor in order:
261	            if neighbor in previous:
262	                continue
263	            if residual.get(node, {}).get(neighbor, 0) > 0:
264	                previous[neighbor] = node
265	                if neighbor == sink:
266	                    path = [sink]
267	                    while path[-1] is not source:
268	                        path.append(previous[path[-1]])
269	                    path.reverse()
270	                    return path
271	                queue.append(neighbor)
272	    return None
273	
274	
275	def seeded_order(digests: Sequence[str], seed: int) -> list[str]:
276	    """Deterministic seed-driven order of the given digests.
277	
278	    Each digest gets a sort key ``H(seed || digest)`` from SHA-256, with
279	    the digest itself breaking ties.  Unlike :mod:`random`, this stream is
280	    defined by the hash algorithm itself, so it is stable across Python
281	    versions and only depends on the digest set and the seed.
282	    """
283	    seed_bytes = str(seed).encode("utf-8")
284	    return sorted(
285	        digests,
286	        key=lambda digest: (
287	            hashlib.sha256(seed_bytes + digest.encode("utf-8")).digest(),
288	            digest,
289	        ),
290	    )
291	
292	
293	def assign(samples: Sequence[dict[str, Any]], ratios: Sequence[Any], seed: Any) -> dict[str, str]:
294	    """Return ``{digest: set_name}`` for the given manifest-like samples.
295	
296	    Each sample mapping must contain ``sha256`` and ``label`` keys.
297	    """
298	    if isinstance(seed, bool) or not isinstance(seed, int):
299	        raise SplitError(f"Seed must be an integer, got {seed!r}")
300	    ratio_values = validate_ratios(ratios)
301	
302	    digests: list[str] = []
303	    seen: set[str] = set()
304	    strata_counts: dict[Any, int] = {}
305	    stratum_of: dict[str, Any] = {}
306	    for sample in samples:
307	        if not isinstance(sample, dict):
308	            raise SplitError("Every sample record must be an object")
309	        digest = sample.get("sha256")
310	        if not isinstance(digest, str) or not digest:
311	            raise SplitError("Every sample needs a non-empty 'sha256' identity")
312	        if digest in seen:
313	            raise SplitError(f"Duplicate sample identity in manifest: {digest}")
314	        seen.add(digest)
315	        key = category_key(sample.get("label"))
316	        stratum_of[digest] = key
317	        strata_counts[key] = strata_counts.get(key, 0) + 1
318	        digests.append(digest)
319	
320	    table = allocation_table(strata_counts, ratio_values)
321	    positions = {digest: i for i, digest in enumerate(seeded_order(digests, seed))}
322	
323	    assignment: dict[str, str] = {}
324	    for key, row in table.items():
325	        members = sorted(
326	            (d for d in digests if stratum_of[d] == key),
327	            key=lambda d: positions[d],
328	        )
329	        start = 0
330	        for j, count in enumerate(row):
331	            for digest in members[start : start + count]:
332	                assignment[digest] = SET_NAMES[j]
333	            start += count
334	    return assignment

from pathlib import Path

from vision_workbench.splits import SET_NAMES, SplitError
from vision_workbench.store import DatasetStore

REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]


class StoreHarness(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self) -> None:
        self.temp = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.root = Path(self.temp.name) / "dataset"
        self.store = DatasetStore(self.root)
        self.store.initialize()
        self._serial = 0

    def tearDown(self) -> None:
        self.temp.cleanup()

    def add_sample(self, label: str | None, content: bytes | None = None) -> str:
        self._serial += 1
        path = self.root.parent / f"sample-{self._serial}.jpg"
        path.write_bytes(content if content is not None else f"content-{self._serial}".encode())
        result = self.store.add(path, label)
        self.assertTrue(result.added)
        return result.digest


class SplitPlanStoreTest(StoreHarness):
    def test_create_reports_counts_and_distributions(self) -> None:
        for _ in range(5):
            self.add_sample("cat")
        for _ in range(3):
            self.add_sample("dog")
        result = self.store.create_split("v1", 42, ["0.6", "0.2", "0.2"])
        self.assertTrue(result.created)
        plan = result.plan
        self.assertEqual(plan["name"], "v1")
        self.assertEqual(plan["seed"], 42)
        self.assertEqual(plan["ratios"], {"train": "3/5", "validation": "1/5", "test": "1/5"})
        self.assertEqual(plan["samples"]["total"], 8)
        totals = {name: plan["sets"][name]["samples"] for name in SET_NAMES}
        self.assertEqual(sum(totals.values()), 8)
        self.assertEqual(totals["train"], 5)
        # Stratification: each set has the same 5:3 shape within <1.
        for name in SET_NAMES:
            dist = plan["sets"][name]["distribution"]
            self.assertEqual(
                dist["cat"] + dist.get("dog", 0), plan["sets"][name]["samples"]
            )

    def test_reuse_vs_conflict(self) -> None:
        self.add_sample("cat")
        self.add_sample("dog")
        first = self.store.create_split("p", 1, [0.5, 0.5, 0])
        self.assertTrue(first.created)
        again = self.store.create_split("p", 1, [0.5, 0.5, 0])
        self.assertFalse(again.created)
        self.assertEqual(again.plan, first.plan)

        with self.assertRaises(SplitError):
            self.store.create_split("p", 2, [0.5, 0.5, 0])
        with self.assertRaises(SplitError):
            self.store.create_split("p", 1, [0.6, 0.4, 0])

        # Conflict must not overwrite the original.
        unchanged = self.store.get_split("p")
        self.assertEqual(unchanged["seed"], 1)
        self.assertEqual(unchanged["ratios"]["train"], "1/2")

        # Importing new samples then re-creating with the same name conflicts.
        self.add_sample("bird")
        with self.assertRaises(SplitError):
            self.store.create_split("p", 1, [0.5, 0.5, 0])

    def test_plan_is_fixed_after_new_imports_and_uses_old_labels(self) -> None:
        d1 = self.add_sample("cat")
        plan = self.store.create_split("fixed", 0, [1, 0, 0]).plan
        d2 = self.add_sample("dog")
        viewed = self.store.get_split("fixed")
        identities = {
            member["sha256"]

            for member in set_payload["members"]

        self.assertEqual(identities, {d1})
        self.assertNotIn(d2, identities)
        self.assertEqual(viewed["samples"], {"total": 1, "distribution": {"cat": 1}})

        # Source file moved/deleted: the plan still loads unchanged.
        source = Path(viewed["sets"]["train"]["members"][0]["source"])

    def test_relocated_workspace_and_restart_keep_assignments(self) -> None:
        digests = []
        for label, count in [("a", 4), ("b", 3), ("c", 2)]:

                digests.append(self.add_sample(label))

        copy_root = self.root.parent / "copied"
        shutil.copytree(self.root, copy_root)

        for set_name in SET_NAMES:

            self.assertEqual(digests, sorted(digests))

        for bad in ["", "  ", "a/b", "a\\b", ".", ".."]:

                self.store.create_split(bad, 0, [1, 0, 0])

    def test_bad_ratios_and_seed_leave_no_plan_or_manifest_change(self) -> None:
        self.add_sample("cat")

            self.assertEqual(leftovers, [])

        plan_path = self.store.splits_directory / "ok.json"
        payload = json.loads(plan_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        # Drop a required field.

        plan_path.write_text(json.dumps(payload), encoding="utf-8")

from __future__ import annotations

import tempfile
import unittest
from pathlib import Path

from vision_workbench.store import DatasetStore


class DatasetStoreTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_add_is_idempotent_and_summary_counts_labels(self) -> None:
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
            root = Path(directory)
            image = root / "sample.jpg"
            image.write_bytes(b"sample-image")
            store = DatasetStore(root / "dataset")

            first = store.add(image, "cat")
            second = store.add(image, "cat")

            self.assertTrue(first.added)
            self.assertFalse(second.added)
            self.assertEqual(first.digest, second.digest)
            self.assertEqual(
                store.summary(),
                {"items": 1, "bytes": 12, "labels": {"cat": 1}},
            )

    def test_empty_summary_initializes_workspace(self) -> None:
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
            store = DatasetStore(Path(directory) / "dataset")
            self.assertEqual(store.summary(), {"items": 0, "bytes": 0, "labels": {}})


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

from __future__ import annotations

import unittest
from fractions import Fraction

from vision_workbench.splits import (
    SET_NAMES,
    SplitError,
    allocation_table,
    assign,
    category_key,
    category_name,
    parse_ratio,
    seeded_order,
    validate_name,
    validate_ratios,
)


def samples(counts: dict[str | object, int]) -> list[dict]:
    """Build manifest-like samples; key None means the unlabeled stratum."""
    built: list[dict] = []
    serial = 0
    for label, count in counts.items():
        for _ in range(count):
            serial += 1
            digest = f"{serial:08d}"
            built.append({"sha256": digest, "label": None if label is None else label})
    return built


class AllocationPropertyTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def assertMarginalBounds(
        self, counts: dict, ratios: tuple[Fraction, Fraction, Fraction]
    ) -> None:
        table = allocation_table(counts, ratios)
        total = sum(counts.values())
        for key, n_c in counts.items():
            row = table[key]
            self.assertEqual(sum(row), n_c)
            for j, ratio in enumerate(ratios):
                expected = Fraction(n_c) * ratio
                self.assertLess(
                    abs(Fraction(row[j]) - expected),
                    1,
                    f"class row {key} set {SET_NAMES[j]}: {row[j]} vs {expected}",
                )
        for j, ratio in enumerate(ratios):
            column = sum(table[key][j] for key in counts)
            expected = Fraction(total) * ratio
            self.assertLess(
                abs(Fraction(column) - expected),
                1,
                f"total set {SET_NAMES[j]}: {column} vs {expected}",
            )

    def test_many_distributions_and_ratios(self) -> None:
        ratio_sets = [
            (Fraction(1, 3), Fraction(1, 3), Fraction(1, 3)),
            (Fraction(7, 10), Fraction(2, 10), Fraction(1, 10)),
            (Fraction(0), Fraction(0), Fraction(1)),
            (Fraction(1), Fraction(0), Fraction(0)),
            (Fraction(0), Fraction(1, 2), Fraction(1, 2)),
            (Fraction(1, 7), Fraction(2, 7), Fraction(4, 7)),
            (Fraction(1, 2), Fraction(1, 3), Fraction(1, 6)),
        ]
        distributions = [
            {"a": 1},
            {"a": 1, "b": 1},
            {"a": 2},
            {"a": 1, "b": 1, "c": 1},
            {"a": 2, "b": 1},
            {"a": 3, "b": 2, "c": 1},
            {"a": 5, "b": 7, "c": 11, "d": 1},
            {str(i): 1 for i in range(20)},
            {"a": 1, "b": 2, "c": 4, "d": 8},
            {"x": 100, "y": 1},
            {"x": 100, "y": 2},
            {str(k): (k % 5) + 1 for k in range(12)},
        ]
        for counts in distributions:
            for ratios in ratio_sets:
                with self.subTest(counts=counts, ratios=ratios):
                    self.assertMarginalBounds(counts, ratios)

    def test_single_sample_classes_with_thirds(self) -> None:
        # Every class has one sample; totals must still stay within <1.
        counts = {f"c{i}": 1 for i in range(10)}
        table = allocation_table(
            counts, (Fraction(1, 3), Fraction(1, 3), Fraction(1, 3))
        )
        totals = [sum(table[c][j] for c in counts) for j in range(3)]
        self.assertEqual(sum(totals), 10)
        for j in range(3):
            self.assertLess(abs(Fraction(totals[j]) - Fraction(10, 3)), 1)

    def test_empty_dataset(self) -> None:
        table = allocation_table(
            {}, (Fraction(1, 3), Fraction(1, 3), Fraction(1, 3))
        )
        self.assertEqual(table, {})


class AssignTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_partition_and_zero_sets_empty(self) -> None:
        data = samples({"a": 4, "b": 3})
        assignment = assign(data, [0, Fraction(1, 2), Fraction(1, 2)], seed=7)
        self.assertEqual(set(assignment), {s["sha256"] for s in data})
        self.assertNotIn("train", set(assignment.values()))
        self.assertTrue(all(value in SET_NAMES for value in assignment.values()))

    def test_unlabeled_distinct_from_literal_class(self) -> None:
        data = [
            {"sha256": "1", "label": None},
            {"sha256": "2", "label": ""},
            {"sha256": "3", "label": "unlabeled"},
        ]
        assignment = assign(data, [1, 0, 0], seed=0)
        self.assertEqual(set(assignment.values()), {"train"})
        # None and "" share a stratum; the literal label is its own stratum.
        self.assertIs(category_key(None), category_key(""))
        self.assertIsNot(category_key("unlabeled"), category_key(None))
        self.assertEqual(category_name(category_key(None)), "")
        self.assertEqual(category_name(category_key("unlabeled")), "unlabeled")

    def test_deterministic_regardless_of_order(self) -> None:
        data = samples({"a": 6, "b": 5, "c": 3})
        first = assign(data, [0.7, 0.2, 0.1], seed=42)
        reordered = list(reversed(data))
        second = assign(reordered, ["0.7", "0.2", "0.1"], seed=42)
        self.assertEqual(first, second)

    def test_seed_changes_selection_on_larger_dataset(self) -> None:
        data = samples({f"c{k}": 6 for k in range(8)})
        ratios = [Fraction(8, 10), Fraction(1, 10), Fraction(1, 10)]
        assignments = {
            seed: tuple(sorted((d, a[d]) for d in (s["sha256"] for s in data)))
            for seed, a in ((s, assign(data, ratios, s)) for s in range(6))
        }
        # At least two seeds must pick different samples for the small sets.
        self.assertGreater(len(set(assignments.values())), 1)

    def test_small_dataset_seed_may_be_identical(self) -> None:
        data = samples({"a": 1})
        self.assertEqual(
            assign(data, [1, 0, 0], seed=0), assign(data, [1, 0, 0], seed=999)
        )

    def test_seeded_order_only_depends_on_set(self) -> None:
        digests = [f"{i:04d}" for i in range(20)]
        self.assertEqual(
            seeded_order(digests, 5), seeded_order(list(reversed(digests)), 5)
        )
        self.assertEqual(seeded_order(digests, 5), seeded_order(digests, 5))

    def test_duplicate_identity_rejected(self) -> None:
        data = [
            {"sha256": "1", "label": "a"},
            {"sha256": "1", "label": "b"},
        ]
        with self.assertRaises(SplitError):
            assign(data, [1, 0, 0], seed=0)

    def test_missing_identity_rejected(self) -> None:
        with self.assertRaises(SplitError):
            assign([{"label": "a"}], [1, 0, 0], seed=0)


class ValidationTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_ratio_rules(self) -> None:
        self.assertEqual(validate_ratios([0, 1, 0]), (Fraction(0), Fraction(1), Fraction(0)))
        self.assertEqual(parse_ratio("1/3"), Fraction(1, 3))
        self.assertEqual(parse_ratio(0.1), Fraction(1, 10))
        for bad in ["nan", "inf", "-inf", "1.0.0", "abc", -0.01, 1.01]:
            with self.assertRaises(SplitError):
                parse_ratio(bad)
        with self.assertRaises(SplitError):
            parse_ratio(True)
        with self.assertRaises(SplitError):
            validate_ratios([0.34, 0.33, 0.32])  # 0.99, not 1
        self.assertEqual(
            validate_ratios(["0.34", "0.33", "0.33"]),
            (Fraction(34, 100), Fraction(33, 100), Fraction(33, 100)),
        )

    def test_seed_must_be_integer(self) -> None:
        with self.assertRaises(SplitError):
            assign([], [1, 0, 0], 1.5)
        with self.assertRaises(SplitError):
            assign([], [1, 0, 0], True)

    def test_name_rules(self) -> None:
        for name in ["ok", "a b", "plan_v2", "..." ]:
            validate_name(name)
        for bad in ["", "   ", "a/b", "a\\b", ".", ".."]:
            with self.assertRaises(SplitError):
                validate_name(bad)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

Now I understand the codebase. Let me plan the implementation.

Requirements (translated from Chinese):

1. **Batch label modification**: User submits a UTF-8 JSON file from the command line, containing a batch number (编号) and a modification list. Each modification specifies a sample by full SHA-256 digest, with expected old label and target label.
   - Batch number must be a non-empty string.
   - Labels can be set, changed, or cleared; `null` and empty string both mean unlabeled; other strings taken literally, including Chinese and a class named "unlabeled".
   - Provide an entry to view current label by digest.
   - On success, report the number of changes; category statistics update accordingly; content digest, source, size unchanged.

2. **Pre-submit verification of entire batch**:
   - Reject the whole batch (no sample changed) if: digest doesn't exist, same sample appears more than once, label is not a string or null, file structure invalid, or any sample's current label doesn't match expected old label.
   - Report reason and locatable record.
   - The two unlabeled spellings (null and "") are considered the same during verification.
   - Records whose target label equals current label count as unchanged; if the whole batch is unchanged, report "no modification needed", don't add to history, and don't occupy the batch number.

3. **Idempotency**:
   - If a successful batch is re-submitted with the same number and content, return the original result without re-modifying, even if someone changed labels afterwards.
   - Adjusting list order or changing unlabeled spelling doesn't count as changed content.
   - Same number with different content → number conflict.

4. **History query**:
   - In successful submission order, show: number, samples involved, labels before/after, and actual changed sample count.
   - Failed batches don't enter history.

5. **Undo by number**:
   - Only if every sample actually modified by that batch has not been modified since, restore all old labels at once.
   - If any one sample was modified afterwards, reject undo, even if it was changed back to the same label.
   - Other samples' subsequent modifications don't block undo.
   - Undo itself leaves a queryable record; repeated undo returns "already undone", doesn't repeatedly write history; unknown number → explicit error.

6. **Concurrency / atomicity**:
   - Two local processes submitting simultaneously must not lose any successful batch; if different batches modify the same sample with the same old label, only one succeeds, the other gets a conflict.
   - After write failure or interruption, reopening the workspace shows only pre-modification or fully-modified labels and corresponding history — no inconsistency between the two.
   - Old workspaces don't need re-import; original command invocation preserved.
   - Label modification and undo don't change saved split members, label snapshots, and distributions; splits created afterwards use current labels; same-name old plans still judge reuse or conflict per original rules.
   - Offline, no third-party runtime deps.

Design:

class BatchError(ValueError): ...

def normalize_label(label):
    if label is None or label == "":
        return None
    if isinstance(label, str):
        return label
    raise BatchError(...)  # callers check types

def validate_batch_payload(data):
    if not isinstance(data, dict):
        raise BatchError("batch file must be a JSON object")
    number = data.get("batch")
    if not isinstance(number, str) or not number.strip():
        raise BatchError("batch number must be a non-empty string")
    changes = data.get("changes")
    if not isinstance(changes, list):
        raise BatchError("'changes' must be a list")
    records = []
    seen = set()
    for i, change in enumerate(changes):
        loc = f"change #{i+1}"
        if not isinstance(change, dict):
            raise BatchError(f"{loc}: must be an object")
        digest = change.get("sha256")
        if not isinstance(digest, str) or not digest:
            raise BatchError(f"{loc}: 'sha256' must be a non-empty string")
        if digest in seen:
            raise BatchError(f"{loc}: duplicate sample {digest}")
        seen.add(digest)
        old = change.get("old")
        new = change.get("new")
        for key, value in (("old", old), ("new", new)):
            if value is not None and not isinstance(value, str):
                raise BatchError(f"{loc}: '{key}' must be a string or null")
        records.append({"sha256": digest, "old": normalize_label(old), "new": normalize_label(new)})
    return number, records
```

def submit_batch(self, path):
    payload = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))  # BatchError on bad JSON
    number, records = validate_batch_payload(payload)
    with self._locked_transaction() as txn:
        # txn provides current manifest + batches, and a commit function
        manifest = txn.manifest
        batches = txn.batches
        items = {item["sha256"]: item for item in manifest["items"]}
        # existence
        for rec in records:
            if rec["sha256"] not in items:
                raise BatchError(f"sample not found: {rec['sha256']}")
        # history check
        existing = next((b for b in batches["batches"] if b["batch"] == number), None)
        if existing is not None:
            if self._content_key(existing["records"]) == self._content_key(records):
                return replay result
            raise BatchError(f"batch number {number!r} already used with different content")
        # old-label check
        for rec in records:
            current = normalize_label(items[rec["sha256"]].get("label"))
            if current != rec["old"]:
                raise BatchError(f"change for {digest}: expected old label {show(rec['old'])} but current is {show(current)}")
        # compute changes
        applied = []
        changed_count = 0
        for rec in records:
            item = items[rec["sha256"]]
            current = normalize_label(item.get("label"))
            changed = current != rec["new"]
            rev = item.get("rev", 0)
            if changed:
                item["label"] = rec["new"]
                item["rev"] = rev + 1
                rev = rev + 1
                changed_count += 1
            applied.append({**rec, "changed": changed, "rev": rev})
        if changed_count == 0:
            return no-changes result (no write)
        entry = {"batch": number, "records": applied, "changed_count": changed_count, "undone": False, "undone_at": None}
        batches["batches"].append(entry)
        txn.commit(manifest, batches)
        return applied result
```

```python
"""Batch label-update submission, validation and history."""
from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Any

BATCH_SCHEMA_VERSION = 1


class BatchError(ValueError):
    """A batch submission or undo request is invalid."""


def normalize_label(label: Any) -> str | None:
    """Map the two unlabeled spellings to ``None``; keep strings literal."""
    if label is None or label == "":
        return None
    if isinstance(label, str):
        return label
    raise BatchError(f"label must be a string or null, got {label!r}")


def parse_batch_file(data: Any) -> tuple[str, list[dict[str, Any]]]:
    """Validate a parsed batch payload; return (number, normalized records)."""
    if not isinstance(data, dict):
        raise BatchError("batch file must contain a JSON object")
    number = data.get("batch")
    if not isinstance(number, str) or not number.strip():
        raise BatchError("batch number must be a non-empty string")
    changes = data.get("changes")
    if not isinstance(changes, list):
        raise BatchError("batch file must contain a 'changes' list")
    records: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    seen: set[str] = set()
    for index, change in enumerate(changes):
        location = f"change #{index + 1}"
        if not isinstance(change, dict):
            raise BatchError(f"{location}: must be an object with 'sha256', 'old' and 'new'")
        if not all(key in change for key in ("sha256", "old", "new")):
            raise BatchError(f"{location}: must contain 'sha256', 'old' and 'new'")
        digest = change["sha256"]
        if not isinstance(digest, str) or not digest:
            raise BatchError(f"{location}: 'sha256' must be a non-empty string")
        if digest in seen:
            raise BatchError(f"{location}: duplicate sample {digest}")
        seen.add(digest)
        old = normalize_label(change["old"])
        new = normalize_label(change["new"])
        records.append({"sha256": digest, "old": old, "new": new})
    return number, records


def content_key(records: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> frozenset[tuple[str, str | None, str | None]]:
    """Order- and spelling-insensitive identity of a batch's content."""
    return frozenset((r["sha256"], r["old"], r["new"]) for r in records)


def empty_history() -> dict[str, Any]:
    return {"schema_version": BATCH_SCHEMA_VERSION, "batches": []}


def validate_history(data: Any) -> dict[str, Any]:
    if not isinstance(data, dict) or data.get("schema_version") != BATCH_SCHEMA_VERSION:
        raise BatchError("Unsupported batch history")
    batches = data.get("batches")
    if not isinstance(batches, list):
        raise BatchError("Malformed batch history")
    for entry in batches:
        if not isinstance(entry, dict) or not isinstance(entry.get("batch"), str):
            raise BatchError("Malformed batch history entry")
        if not isinstance(entry.get("records"), list):
            raise BatchError("Malformed batch history entry")
        if not isinstance(entry.get("changed_count"), int) or isinstance(entry["changed_count"], bool):
            raise BatchError("Malformed batch history entry")
        for record in entry["records"]:
            if not isinstance(record, dict):
                raise BatchError("Malformed batch history record")
            if not isinstance(record.get("sha256"), str):
                raise BatchError("Malformed batch history record")
            for key in ("old", "new"):
                value = record.get(key)
                if value is not None and not isinstance(value, str):
                    raise BatchError("Malformed batch history record")
            if not isinstance(record.get("changed"), bool):
                raise BatchError("Malformed batch history record")
    return data
```

def submit_batch_file(self, path):
    path = Path(path)
    try:
        data = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError) as error:
        raise BatchError(f"cannot read batch file: {error}") from error

def submit_batch(self, data):
    number, records = parse_batch_file(data)
    with self._workspace_lock():
        self._recover_transaction_locked()
        manifest = self._read()
        history = self._read_history()
        items = {item["sha256"]: item for item in manifest["items"]}
        for record in records:
            if record["sha256"] not in items:
                raise BatchError(f"sample not found: {record['sha256']}")
        entries = history["batches"]
        existing = next((e for e in entries if e["batch"] == number), None)
        if existing is not None:
            if content_key(existing["records"]) == content_key(records):
                return self._replay_result(existing)
            raise BatchError(f"batch number {number!r} is already used with different content")
        for record in records:
            current = normalize_label(items[record["sha256"]].get("label"))
            if current != record["old"]:
                raise BatchError(
                    f"change for {record['sha256']}: expected old label "
                    f"{self._render_label(record['old'])} but current label is "
                    f"{self._render_label(current)}"
                )
        changed_records = []
        changed_count = 0
        for record in records:
            item = items[record["sha256"]]
            current = normalize_label(item.get("label"))
            changed = current != record["new"]
            revision = int(item.get("rev", 0))
            if changed:
                item["label"] = record["new"]
                revision += 1
                item["rev"] = revision
                changed_count += 1
            changed_records.append({**record, "changed": changed, "rev": revision})
        if changed_count == 0:
            return {"batch": number, "status": "no-changes", "changed": 0,
                    "unchanged": len(records), "total": len(records)}
        entry = {
            "batch": number,
            "records": changed_records,
            "changed_count": changed_count,
            "undone": False,
            "undone_at": None,
        }
        entries.append(entry)
        self._commit(manifest, history)
        return {"batch": number, "status": "applied", "changed": changed_count,
                "unchanged": len(records) - changed_count, "total": len(records)}

        self._recover_transaction_locked()
        manifest = self._read()
        history = self._read_history()

            current = normalize_label(item.get("label"))
            if int(item.get("rev", 0)) != record["rev"] or current != record["new"]:
                raise BatchError(
                    f"cannot undo batch {number!r}: sample {record['sha256']} "

        restored = []

            if not record["changed"]:

            item = items[record["sha256"]]
            item["label"] = record["old"]
            item["rev"] = int(item.get("rev", 0)) + 1
            restored.append(record["sha256"])
        entry["undone"] = True
        entry["undone_at"] = datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()
        self._commit(manifest, history)
        return {"batch": number, "status": "undone", "restored": len(restored)}

    except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError) as error:
        raise BatchError(f"cannot recover interrupted transaction: {error}") from error
    manifest = journal.get("manifest")

    self._write_json_atomic(self.manifest_path, manifest)
    self._write_json_atomic(self.batches_path, history)

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

from .store import DatasetStore


def parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
    value = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="vision-workbench")
    commands = value.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True)

    initialize = commands.add_parser("init", help="initialize a dataset workspace")
    initialize.add_argument("workspace", type=Path)

    add = commands.add_parser("add", help="add an image record")
    add.add_argument("workspace", type=Path)
    add.add_argument("source", type=Path)
    add.add_argument("--label")

    summary = commands.add_parser("summary", help="show dataset statistics")
    summary.add_argument("workspace", type=Path)

    split = commands.add_parser(
        "split", help="create and inspect train/validation/test plans"
    )
    split_commands = split.add_subparsers(dest="split_command", required=True)

    create = split_commands.add_parser("create", help="create a named split plan")
    create.add_argument("workspace", type=Path)
    create.add_argument("name", help="plan name (no '/', '\\', '.' or '..')")
    create.add_argument("--seed", type=int, required=True, help="integer random seed")
    create.add_argument("--train", required=True, help="training ratio in [0, 1]")
    create.add_argument("--validation", required=True, help="validation ratio in [0, 1]")
    create.add_argument("--test", required=True, help="test ratio in [0, 1]")

    show = split_commands.add_parser("show", help="show a saved split plan as JSON")
    show.add_argument("workspace", type=Path)
    show.add_argument("name", help="plan name")

    demo = commands.add_parser("demo", help="show a read-only product demonstration")
    demo.add_argument("--workspace", type=Path, default=Path("."))
    return value


def main() -> int:

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import multiprocessing
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import unittest
from pathlib import Path

from vision_workbench.batches import BatchError
from vision_workbench.store import DatasetStore

REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]


class StoreHarness(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self) -> None:
        self.temp = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.root = Path(self.temp.name) / "dataset"
        self.store = DatasetStore(self.root)
        self.store.initialize()
        self._serial = 0

    def tearDown(self) -> None:
        self.temp.cleanup()

    def add_sample(self, label: str | None, content: bytes | None = None) -> str:
        self._serial += 1
        path = self.root.parent / f"sample-{self._serial}.jpg"
        path.write_bytes(content if content is not None else f"content-{self._serial}".encode())
        result = self.store.add(path, label)
        self.assertTrue(result.added)
        return result.digest

    def submit(self, number: str, *changes: tuple) -> dict:
        """Submit a batch; each change is (digest, old, new)."""
        return self.store.submit_batch(
            {
                "batch": number,
                "changes": [
                    {"sha256": digest, "old": old, "new": new}
                    for digest, old, new in changes
                ],
            }
        )

    def manifest_labels(self) -> dict[str, str | None]:
        manifest = json.loads(self.store.manifest_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        return {item["sha256"]: item.get("label") for item in manifest["items"]}


class BatchSubmitTest(StoreHarness):
    def test_submit_changes_labels_and_summary(self) -> None:
        d1 = self.add_sample("cat")
        d2 = self.add_sample("dog")
        before = json.loads(self.store.manifest_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))

        result = self.submit("b1", (d1, "cat", "kitten"), (d2, "dog", None))
        self.assertEqual(result["status"], "applied")
        self.assertEqual(result["changed"], 2)
        self.assertEqual(result["unchanged"], 0)

        self.assertEqual(self.store.lookup_label(d1)["label"], "kitten")
        self.assertIsNone(self.store.lookup_label(d2)["label"])
        summary = self.store.summary()
        self.assertEqual(summary["items"], 2)
        self.assertEqual(summary["labels"], {"kitten": 1, "unlabeled": 1})

        # Content digest, source and size are untouched.
        after = json.loads(self.store.manifest_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        before_items = {i["sha256"]: i for i in before["items"]}
        after_items = {i["sha256"]: i for i in after["items"]}
        for digest, item in after_items.items():
            self.assertEqual(item["source"], before_items[digest]["source"])
            self.assertEqual(item["size"], before_items[digest]["size"])
            self.assertEqual(item["sha256"], before_items[digest]["sha256"])

    def test_null_and_empty_both_unlabeled_literal_unlabeled_kept(self) -> None:
        d1 = self.add_sample("cat")
        d2 = self.add_sample("cat")
        d3 = self.add_sample("cat")
        d4 = self.add_sample("cat")

        # Clear with null, then with the empty string.
        self.submit("b1", (d1, "cat", None))
        self.submit("b2", (d2, "cat", ""))
        self.assertIsNone(self.store.lookup_label(d1)["label"])
        self.assertIsNone(self.store.lookup_label(d2)["label"])

        # A real class literally named "unlabeled" stays distinct.
        self.submit("b3", (d3, "cat", "unlabeled"))
        self.assertEqual(self.store.lookup_label(d3)["label"], "unlabeled")

        # Chinese labels are taken literally.
        self.submit("b4", (d4, "cat", "猫"))
        self.assertEqual(self.store.lookup_label(d4)["label"], "猫")

        summary = self.store.summary()
        self.assertEqual(summary["labels"], {"unlabeled": 2, "猫": 1, "cat": 1})

    def test_set_label_on_unlabeled_sample(self) -> None:
        d = self.add_sample(None)
        result = self.submit("b1", (d, None, "cat"))
        self.assertEqual(result["status"], "applied")
        self.assertEqual(self.store.lookup_label(d)["label"], "cat")

    def test_noop_batch_reports_no_changes_and_occupies_no_number(self) -> None:
        d = self.add_sample("cat")
        result = self.submit("b1", (d, "cat", "cat"))
        self.assertEqual(result["status"], "no-changes")
        self.assertEqual(result["changed"], 0)
        self.assertEqual(self.store.history(), [])

        # The number is still free for a real batch.
        real = self.submit("b1", (d, "cat", "dog"))
        self.assertEqual(real["status"], "applied")
        self.assertEqual(self.store.history()[0]["batch"], "b1")

    def test_empty_changes_list_is_noop(self) -> None:
        result = self.store.submit_batch({"batch": "empty", "changes": []})
        self.assertEqual(result["status"], "no-changes")
        self.assertEqual(self.store.history(), [])

    def test_replay_returns_original_result_without_remodifying(self) -> None:
        d = self.add_sample("cat")
        first = self.submit("b1", (d, "cat", "dog"))
        self.assertEqual(first["status"], "applied")

        # Someone changes the label back; the expected old label no longer
        # matches, but replay must still return the original result.
        self.submit("b2", (d, "dog", "cat"))
        replay = self.submit("b1", (d, "cat", "dog"))
        self.assertEqual(replay["status"], "already-applied")
        self.assertEqual(replay["changed"], first["changed"])
        self.assertEqual(replay["batch"], first["batch"])
        # The replay did not modify anything (label stays cat).
        self.assertEqual(self.store.lookup_label(d)["label"], "cat")

    def test_replay_order_and_unlabeled_spelling_are_irrelevant(self) -> None:
        d1 = self.add_sample(None)
        d2 = self.add_sample("")
        self.submit("b1", (d1, None, "cat"), (d2, None, "dog"))

        # Reversed order, "" instead of null for old labels.
        replay = self.store.submit_batch(
            {
                "batch": "b1",
                "changes": [
                    {"sha256": d2, "old": "", "new": "dog"},
                    {"sha256": d1, "old": "", "new": "cat"},
                ],
            }
        )
        self.assertEqual(replay["status"], "already-applied")

    def test_same_number_different_content_conflicts(self) -> None:
        d = self.add_sample("cat")
        self.submit("b1", (d, "cat", "dog"))
        with self.assertRaises(BatchError):
            self.submit("b1", (d, "cat", "fish"))
        # History keeps the original batch only.
        self.assertEqual([e["batch"] for e in self.store.history()], ["b1"])
        self.assertEqual(self.store.lookup_label(d)["label"], "dog")

    def test_history_lists_successes_in_submission_order(self) -> None:
        d1 = self.add_sample("cat")
        d2 = self.add_sample("dog")
        self.submit("a1", (d1, "cat", "kitten"))
        self.submit("a2", (d2, "dog", None))
        history = self.store.history()
        self.assertEqual([e["batch"] for e in history], ["a1", "a2"])
        self.assertEqual(history[0]["changed_count"], 1)
        self.assertEqual(history[0]["records"][0]["old"], "cat")
        self.assertEqual(history[0]["records"][0]["new"], "kitten")
        self.assertEqual(history[1]["records"][0]["old"], "dog")
        self.assertIsNone(history[1]["records"][0]["new"])
        self.assertFalse(history[0]["undone"])

    def test_failed_batch_enters_no_history(self) -> None:
        d = self.add_sample("cat")
        with self.assertRaises(BatchError):
            self.submit("bad", (d, "cat", "dog"), ("deadbeef", "cat", "dog"))
        self.assertEqual(self.store.history(), [])
        self.assertEqual(self.store.lookup_label(d)["label"], "cat")


class BatchValidationTest(StoreHarness):
    def assert_rejected(self, data: object) -> None:
        with self.assertRaises(BatchError):
            self.store.submit_batch(data)
        self.assertEqual(self.store.history(), [])

    def test_file_must_be_object(self) -> None:
        self.assert_rejected(["not", "an", "object"])

    def test_batch_number_must_be_nonempty_string(self) -> None:
        d = self.add_sample("cat")
        for bad in [None, "", "   ", 123]:
            self.assert_rejected({"batch": bad, "changes": [
                {"sha256": d, "old": "cat", "new": "dog"}]})

    def test_changes_must_be_list(self) -> None:
        self.assert_rejected({"batch": "b", "changes": {}})

    def test_change_must_have_required_keys(self) -> None:
        d = self.add_sample("cat")
        self.assert_rejected({"batch": "b", "changes": [
            {"sha256": d, "old": "cat"}]})
        self.assert_rejected({"batch": "b", "changes": [
            {"sha256": d, "new": "dog"}]})

    def test_digest_must_be_nonempty_string(self) -> None:
        self.assert_rejected({"batch": "b", "changes": [
            {"sha256": "", "old": "cat", "new": "dog"}]})
        self.assert_rejected({"batch": "b", "changes": [
            {"sha256": 123, "old": "cat", "new": "dog"}]})

    def test_label_must_be_string_or_null(self) -> None:
        d = self.add_sample("cat")
        for bad_old in [123, True, ["cat"], {"cat": 1}]:
            self.assert_rejected({"batch": "b", "changes": [
                {"sha256": d, "old": bad_old, "new": "dog"}]})
        for bad_new in [123, True, ["dog"]]:
            self.assert_rejected({"batch": "b", "changes": [
                {"sha256": d, "old": "cat", "new": bad_new}]})

    def test_missing_digest_rejects_whole_batch(self) -> None:
        d = self.add_sample("cat")
        with self.assertRaises(BatchError) as ctx:
            self.submit("b", (d, "cat", "dog"), ("f" * 64, "cat", "fish"))
        self.assertIn("not found", str(ctx.exception))
        # Nothing changed.
        self.assertEqual(self.store.lookup_label(d)["label"], "cat")

    def test_duplicate_digest_rejects_whole_batch(self) -> None:
        d = self.add_sample("cat")
        with self.assertRaises(BatchError) as ctx:
            self.store.submit_batch({"batch": "b", "changes": [
                {"sha256": d, "old": "cat", "new": "dog"},
                {"sha256": d, "old": "cat", "new": "fish"},
            ]})
        self.assertIn("duplicate", str(ctx.exception))
        self.assertEqual(self.store.lookup_label(d)["label"], "cat")

    def test_old_label_mismatch_rejects_whole_batch(self) -> None:
        d1 = self.add_sample("cat")
        d2 = self.add_sample("cat")
        with self.assertRaises(BatchError) as ctx:
            self.submit("b", (d1, "cat", "dog"), (d2, "kitten", "fish"))
        message = str(ctx.exception)
        self.assertIn(d2, message)
        self.assertIn("kitten", message)
        self.assertIn("cat", message)
        # Neither sample changed.
        self.assertEqual(self.store.lookup_label(d1)["label"], "cat")
        self.assertEqual(self.store.lookup_label(d2)["label"], "cat")

    def test_null_and_empty_spellings_match_as_old_labels(self) -> None:
        d1 = self.add_sample(None)
        d2 = self.add_sample("")
        # Expected old label "" matches a sample stored as null.
        result = self.store.submit_batch({"batch": "b", "changes": [
            {"sha256": d1, "old": "", "new": "cat"},
            {"sha256": d2, "old": None, "new": "dog"},
        ]})
        self.assertEqual(result["status"], "applied")

    def test_malformed_json_file_rejected(self) -> None:
        d = self.add_sample("cat")
        batch_path = self.root.parent / "bad.json"
        batch_path.write_text("{not json", encoding="utf-8")
        with self.assertRaises(BatchError):
            self.store.submit_batch_file(batch_path)
        self.assertEqual(self.store.lookup_label(d)["label"], "cat")


class BatchUndoTest(StoreHarness):
    def test_undo_restores_old_labels(self) -> None:
        d1 = self.add_sample("cat")
        d2 = self.add_sample("dog")
        self.submit("b1", (d1, "cat", "kitten"), (d2, "dog", None))
        result = self.store.undo_batch("b1")
        self.assertEqual(result["status"], "undone")
        self.assertEqual(result["restored"], 2)
        self.assertEqual(self.store.lookup_label(d1)["label"], "cat")
        self.assertEqual(self.store.lookup_label(d2)["label"], "dog")
        history = self.store.history()
        self.assertTrue(history[0]["undone"])
        self.assertIsNotNone(history[0]["undone_at"])

    def test_undo_only_changed_samples_checked(self) -> None:
        d1 = self.add_sample("cat")
        d2 = self.add_sample("dog")
        # d2 is a no-op in b1.
        self.submit("b1", (d1, "cat", "kitten"), (d2, "dog", "dog"))
        # Modify d2 afterwards; it should not block undo of b1.
        self.submit("b2", (d2, "dog", "fish"))
        result = self.store.undo_batch("b1")
        self.assertEqual(result["status"], "undone")
        self.assertEqual(result["restored"], 1)
        self.assertEqual(self.store.lookup_label(d1)["label"], "cat")
        self.assertEqual(self.store.lookup_label(d2)["label"], "fish")

    def test_undo_rejected_when_sample_modified_afterwards(self) -> None:
        d1 = self.add_sample("cat")
        d2 = self.add_sample("dog")
        self.submit("b1", (d1, "cat", "kitten"), (d2, "dog", "puppy"))
        self.submit("b2", (d2, "puppy", "fish"))
        with self.assertRaises(BatchError) as ctx:
            self.store.undo_batch("b1")
        self.assertIn("modified after", str(ctx.exception))
        # Nothing undone.
        self.assertFalse(self.store.history()[0]["undone"])
        self.assertEqual(self.store.lookup_label(d1)["label"], "kitten")
        self.assertEqual(self.store.lookup_label(d2)["label"], "fish")

    def test_undo_rejected_even_if_label_changed_back(self) -> None:
        d = self.add_sample("cat")
        self.submit("b1", (d, "cat", "dog"))
        self.submit("b2", (d, "dog", "cat"))
        with self.assertRaises(BatchError):
            self.store.undo_batch("b1")

    def test_repeated_undo_is_idempotent(self) -> None:
        d = self.add_sample("cat")
        self.submit("b1", (d, "cat", "dog"))
        first = self.store.undo_batch("b1")

    def test_unknown_batch_number_rejected(self) -> None:

    def test_undo_then_new_batch_works(self) -> None:

def _submit_worker(root: str, number: str, changes: list, queue) -> None:
    try:
        store = DatasetStore(Path(root))
        result = store.submit_batch(
            {"batch": number, "changes": changes}
        )
        queue.put(("ok", result))
    except Exception as error:  # noqa: BLE001 - report back to parent
        queue.put(("error", str(error)))


class BatchConcurrencyTest(StoreHarness):
    def test_concurrent_both_succeed(self) -> None:

        d2 = self.add_sample("cat")
        ctx = multiprocessing.get_context("fork")
        queue = ctx.Queue()
        p1 = ctx.Process(
            target=_submit_worker,
            args=(str(self.root), "b1",
                  [{"sha256": d1, "old": "cat", "new": "dog"}], queue),
        )
        p2 = ctx.Process(
            target=_submit_worker,
            args=(str(self.root), "b2",
                  [{"sha256": d2, "old": "cat", "new": "fish"}], queue),
        )
        p1.start()
        p2.start()
        p1.join()
        p2.join()
        results = [queue.get_nowait(), queue.get_nowait()]
        self.assertEqual({status for status, _ in results}, {"ok"})
        labels = self.manifest_labels()
        self.assertEqual(labels[d1], "dog")
        self.assertEqual(labels[d2], "fish")
        self.assertEqual(
            sorted(e["batch"] for e in self.store.history()), ["b1", "b2"]
        )

    def test_concurrent_same_batch_is_idempotent(self) -> None:
        d = self.add_sample("cat")
        ctx = multiprocessing.get_context("fork")
        queue = ctx.Queue()
        changes = [{"sha256": d, "old": "cat", "new": "dog"}]
        processes = [
            ctx.Process(target=_submit_worker,
                        args=(str(self.root), "b1", changes, queue))
            for _ in range(2)
        ]
        for process in processes:
            process.start()
        for process in processes:
            process.join()
        results = [queue.get_nowait(), queue.get_nowait()]
        self.assertEqual({status for status, _ in results}, {"ok"})
        statuses = {payload["status"] for _, payload in results}
        self.assertEqual(statuses, {"applied", "already-applied"})
        self.assertEqual(self.store.lookup_label(d)["label"], "dog")
        self.assertEqual(len(self.store.history()), 1)

    def test_concurrent_conflicting_batches_one_succeeds(self) -> None:
        d = self.add_sample("cat")
        ctx = multiprocessing.get_context("fork")
        queue = ctx.Queue()
        p1 = ctx.Process(
            target=_submit_worker,
            args=(str(self.root), "b1",
                  [{"sha256": d, "old": "cat", "new": "dog"}], queue),
        )
        p2 = ctx.Process(
            target=_submit_worker,
            args=(str(self.root), "b2",
                  [{"sha256": d, "old": "cat", "new": "fish"}], queue),
        )
        p1.start()
        p2.start()
        p1.join()
        p2.join()
        results = [queue.get_nowait(), queue.get_nowait()]
        statuses = [status for status, _ in results]
        self.assertIn("ok", statuses)
        self.assertIn("error", statuses)
        winner = next(payload for status, payload in results if status == "ok")
        loser_message = next(
            message for status, message in results if status == "error"
        )
        self.assertIn("expected old label", loser_message)
        self.assertEqual(winner["changed"], 1)
        # Exactly one label change landed, history has exactly one batch.
        self.assertEqual(self.store.lookup_label(d)["label"], winner["batch"] and "dog"
                         if winner["batch"] == "b1" else "fish")
        self.assertEqual(len(self.store.history()), 1)

class StoreHarness(unittest.TestCase):

        self.store.initialize()
        self._serial = 0

    def add_sample(self, label: str | None, content: bytes | None = None) -> str:
        self._serial += 1
        path = self.root.parent / f"sample-{self._serial}.jpg"
        path.write_bytes(content if content is not None else f"content-{self._serial}".encode())
        result = self.store.add(path, label)
        self.assertTrue(result.added)
        return result.digest

    def submit(self, number: str, *changes: tuple) -> dict:
        """Submit a batch; each change is (digest, old, new)."""
        return self.store.submit_batch(
            {
                "batch": number,
                "changes": [
                    {"sha256": digest, "old": old, "new": new}
                    for digest, old, new in changes
                ],
            }
        )

    def manifest_labels(self) -> dict[str, str | None]:
        manifest = json.loads(self.store.manifest_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        return {item["sha256"]: item.get("label") for item in manifest["items"]}

def _submit_worker(root: str, number: str, changes: list, queue) -> None:
    try:
        store = DatasetStore(Path(root))
        result = store.submit_batch(
            {"batch": number, "changes": changes}
        )
        queue.put(("ok", result))
    except Exception as error:  # noqa: BLE001 - report back to parent
        queue.put(("error", str(error)))


class BatchConcurrencyTest(StoreHarness):
    def test_concurrent_both_succeed(self) -> None:
        d1 = self.add_sample("cat")
        d2 = self.add_sample("cat")
        ctx = multiprocessing.get_context("fork")
        queue = ctx.Queue()
        p1 = ctx.Process(
            target=_submit_worker,
            args=(str(self.root), "b1",
                  [{"sha256": d1, "old": "cat", "new": "dog"}], queue),
        )
        p2 = ctx.Process(
            target=_submit_worker,
            args=(str(self.root), "b2",
                  [{"sha256": d2, "old": "cat", "new": "fish"}], queue),
        )
        p1.start()
        p2.start()
        p1.join()
        p2.join()
        results = [queue.get_nowait(), queue.get_nowait()]
        self.assertEqual({status for status, _ in results}, {"ok"})
        labels = self.manifest_labels()
        self.assertEqual(labels[d1], "dog")
        self.assertEqual(labels[d2], "fish")
        self.assertEqual(
            sorted(e["batch"] for e in self.store.history()), ["b1", "b2"]
        )

    def test_concurrent_same_batch_is_idempotent(self) -> None:
        d = self.add_sample("cat")
        ctx = multiprocessing.get_context("fork")
        queue = ctx.Queue()
        changes = [{"sha256": d, "old": "cat", "new": "dog"}]
        processes = [
            ctx.Process(target=_submit_worker,
                        args=(str(self.root), "b1", changes, queue))
            for _ in range(2)
        ]
        for process in processes:
            process.start()
        for process in processes:
            process.join()
        results = [queue.get_nowait(), queue.get_nowait()]
        self.assertEqual({status for status, _ in results}, {"ok"})
        statuses = {payload["status"] for _, payload in results}
        self.assertEqual(statuses, {"applied", "already-applied"})
        self.assertEqual(self.store.lookup_label(d)["label"], "dog")
        self.assertEqual(len(self.store.history()), 1)

    def test_concurrent_conflicting_batches_one_succeeds(self) -> None:
        d = self.add_sample("cat")
        ctx = multiprocessing.get_context("fork")
        queue = ctx.Queue()
        p1 = ctx.Process(
            target=_submit_worker,
            args=(str(self.root), "b1",
                  [{"sha256": d, "old": "cat", "new": "dog"}], queue),
        )
        p2 = ctx.Process(
            target=_submit_worker,
            args=(str(self.root), "b2",
                  [{"sha256": d, "old": "cat", "new": "fish"}], queue),
        )
        p1.start()
        p2.start()
        p1.join()
        p2.join()
        results = [queue.get_nowait(), queue.get_nowait()]
        statuses = [status for status, _ in results]
        self.assertIn("ok", statuses)
        self.assertIn("error", statuses)
        winner = next(payload for status, payload in results if status == "ok")
        loser_message = next(
            message for status, message in results if status == "error"
        )
        self.assertIn("expected old label", loser_message)
        self.assertEqual(winner["changed"], 1)
        # Exactly one label change landed, history has exactly one batch.
        self.assertEqual(self.store.lookup_label(d)["label"], winner["batch"] and "dog"
                         if winner["batch"] == "b1" else "fish")
        self.assertEqual(len(self.store.history()), 1)
